title: Modal verbs (presente): elegí el correcto
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. Primero identificá la categoría: obligación, consejo, prohibición, deducción, habilidad, permiso, falta de necesidad.

items.q: You ___ back up your files regularly to avoid losing important data.
items.e: Consejo en presente → should. 'should have' es crítica sobre el pasado.

should have: should have + participio es un reproche sobre el PASADO; acá es un consejo para ahora: should.
mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; acá es un consejo (conviene hacer backups): should.
can't: significado
can't = no se puede / es imposible; no expresa un consejo: should.

items.q: The server is down. The IT team ___ be working on it now.
items.e: Deducción positiva casi segura → must be.

can't: significado
can't expresa que algo es imposible (deducción negativa); acá se deduce que SÍ lo están arreglando: must.
mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; no sirve para deducir: must.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; no expresa deducción: must.

items.q: You ___ use your colleague's password without permission.

don't have to: don't have to = no es necesario (está permitido no hacerlo). Usar la clave de otro está PROHIBIDO: mustn't.
can't be: can't be expresa deducción negativa y va con un adjetivo/sustantivo; acá hay un verbo (use) y es una prohibición: mustn't.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; no expresa prohibición: mustn't.

items.q: We ___ finish the report today. The deadline is next week.
items.e: No es necesario → don't have to (no prohibido).

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido. La fecha límite es la semana próxima, así que no hay obligación: don't have to.
can't: significado
can't = no se puede / imposible; acá se dice que no es necesario hacerlo hoy: don't have to.
must: must = obligación; el deadline es la semana próxima, así que no es obligatorio hoy: don't have to.

items.q: You ___ install that program. It may contain malware.

don't have to: don't have to = no es necesario. Acá hay una advertencia de riesgo (malware): shouldn't.
can't be: can't be expresa deducción y va con adjetivo/sustantivo; acá hay un verbo y un consejo negativo: shouldn't.
must be: must be expresa deducción y va con adjetivo/sustantivo; acá hay un verbo y un consejo negativo: shouldn't.

items.q: The developer isn't answering his phone. He ___ be in a meeting.
items.e: Posibilidad presente (no hay certeza) → might/may/could + base.

must have: must have necesita un participio (must have been) y habla del pasado; acá es una posibilidad ahora: might.
should have: should have + participio es un reproche sobre el pasado; acá es una posibilidad ahora: might.
ought to have: ought to have + participio es un reproche sobre el pasado; acá es una posibilidad ahora: might.

items.q: She ___ be a beginner. She fixed that bug in five minutes.
items.e: Deducción negativa → can't be, nunca mustn't be.

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; para deducir que algo es imposible se usa can't.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; no expresa deducción: can't.
shouldn't: shouldn't = no conviene (consejo); no expresa deducción: can't.

items.q: The company says all employees ___ change their passwords every 90 days.
items.e: Regla externa de la empresa → have to.

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; la regla de la empresa es una obligación: have to.
can't: significado
can't = no se puede; la regla de la empresa es una obligación: have to.
could: could = podría (posibilidad/habilidad); una regla de la empresa es una obligación: have to.

items.q: You ___ pay for this software. It's open-source.

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; acá es 'no es necesario' (es open-source): don't have to.
can't: significado
can't = no se puede; daría 'es imposible pagar'. La idea es que no es necesario: don't have to.
shouldn't have: shouldn't have + participio es un reproche sobre el pasado; acá es el presente: don't have to.

items.q: ___ I deploy this to staging now?

Must: Must I...? pregunta por una obligación; para pedir permiso o preguntar si es posible: Can.
Mustn't: Mustn't I...? es una forma rara de preguntar por prohibición; para pedir permiso: Can.
Needn't: Needn't I...? pregunta si no hace falta; para pedir permiso: Can.

items.q: When I started working here, I ___ write code very well, but now I can.

can't: tiempo
can't es presente; When I started habla del pasado: couldn't.
mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; acá se habla de una habilidad que no tenía: couldn't.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; acá se habla de una habilidad que no tenía: couldn't.

items.q: ___ you like some coffee?

Should: Should you like...? no se usa para ofrecer; Would you like...? es la oferta educada.
Must: Must you like...? pregunta por una obligación; la oferta educada es Would you like...?
Might: Might you like...? es muy formal y poco natural; la oferta estándar es Would you like...?

title: Modal verbs: escribí el modal
instructions: Escribí el modal (o semi-modal) que corresponde a la traducción.
text:
1. Tenés que parar en la luz roja (es una regla): You [1] stop at a red light.
2. No hace falta que compres tomates: You [2] buy any tomatoes.
3. Está prohibido fumar acá: You [3] smoke here.
4. Deberías ver a un médico: You [4] see a doctor.
5. No puede ser americano; su inglés es terrible: He [5] be American.
6. Debe ser muy rico; tiene un Rolls Royce: He [6] be very rich.
7. Puede que llueva: It [7] rain.
8. Cuando estaba en la facultad, solía quedarme despierto toda la noche: When I was in college, I [8] stay up all night coding.

pat: should = consejo; 'es una regla' pide obligación: have to (o must).
la estructura completa es have to + verbo.
items.e: Regla externa → have to (must también se acepta).

pat: mustn't = prohibido. 'No hace falta' es ausencia de necesidad: don't have to / needn't.
have to/must = obligación; es lo contrario de 'no hace falta': don't have to.
items.e: No es necesario → don't have to / needn't.

pat: don't have to / needn't = no es necesario (se puede no hacerlo). 'Está prohibido' es mustn't.
items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: You can't + verbo también expresa prohibición y es muy común (más informal que mustn't). En el examen, si la consigna pide la prohibición con modal, la forma más típica es mustn't.

pat: must/have to = obligación; 'deberías' es un consejo: should / ought to.
mustn't = prohibido. Para decir 'es imposible que sea' se usa can't.
items.e: Deducción negativa → can't be (nunca mustn't be).

pat: should/have to = consejo u obligación. Para decir 'seguro que es' se usa must.
must = seguro que sí; can't = seguro que no. 'Puede que llueva' (posible) es might / may / could.
will es presente/futuro; cuando estaba en la facultad habla del pasado: would (hábito repetido) o used to.
items.e: Hábito pasado repetido → would (o used to).

title: ¿Qué expresa el modal?
instructions: Elegí la categoría de la parte en negrita.

items.q: You **must** finish the report.

Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés must finish.
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés must finish.
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés must finish.
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés must finish.
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés must finish.
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés must finish.
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés must finish.

items.q: You **should** see a doctor.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés should see.
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés should see.
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés should see.
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés should see.
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés should see.
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés should see.
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés should see.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés mustn't smoke.

items.q: She **can** code in three languages.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés can code (habilidad).

items.q: He **must be** rich.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés must be rich (deducción).

items.q: It **might** rain.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés might rain (no seguro).

items.q: You **don't have to** buy tomatoes.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés don't have to buy.
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés don't have to buy.

items.q: **Can** I go out?

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés Can I go out? (pedir permiso).

items.q: He **can't be** American.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Lack of necessity: don't have to / needn't = no hace falta. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés can't be American (deducción negativa).

items.q: You **needn't** finish it today.

Obligation: must / have to = obligación o regla. Acá tenés needn't finish.
Advice: should / ought to = consejo. Acá tenés needn't finish.
Prohibition: mustn't / can't = prohibido. Acá tenés needn't finish.
Ability: can / could = habilidad. Acá tenés needn't finish.
Certainty (deduction): must be / can't be = deducción de algo casi seguro. Acá tenés needn't finish.
Possibility: might / may / could = posibilidad (no seguro). Acá tenés needn't finish.
Permission: can / may = pedir o dar permiso. Acá tenés needn't finish.

title: Los usos de would
instructions: Elegí el uso de would en la parte en negrita. Truco: si se traduce con -ía, es would.

items.q: If I had more time, I **would learn** Rust.

Pedido formal / cortesía: Would you...? = pedido u ofrecimiento cortés. Acá tenés If I had more time, I would learn (hipotético).
Opinión suavizada: I would say / I would think = opinión más suave y menos directa. Acá tenés If I had more time, I would learn (hipotético).
Hábito pasado repetido: would + verbo (en pasado) = costumbre repetida de otra época. Acá tenés If I had more time, I would learn (hipotético).

items.q: **Would** you mind closing the door?

Condicional hipotético: would + verbo, con una condición (if) = situación hipotética. Acá tenés Would you mind...? (pedido cortés).
Opinión suavizada: I would say / I would think = opinión más suave y menos directa. Acá tenés Would you mind...? (pedido cortés).
Hábito pasado repetido: would + verbo (en pasado) = costumbre repetida de otra época. Acá tenés Would you mind...? (pedido cortés).

items.q: I **would say** this bug is critical.

Condicional hipotético: would + verbo, con una condición (if) = situación hipotética. Acá tenés I would say (opinión suavizada).
Pedido formal / cortesía: Would you...? = pedido u ofrecimiento cortés. Acá tenés I would say (opinión suavizada).
Hábito pasado repetido: would + verbo (en pasado) = costumbre repetida de otra época. Acá tenés I would say (opinión suavizada).

items.q: When I was in college, I **would stay up** all night coding.

Condicional hipotético: would + verbo, con una condición (if) = situación hipotética. Acá tenés When I was in college, I would stay up (hábito pasado).
Pedido formal / cortesía: Would you...? = pedido u ofrecimiento cortés. Acá tenés When I was in college, I would stay up (hábito pasado).
Opinión suavizada: I would say / I would think = opinión más suave y menos directa. Acá tenés When I was in college, I would stay up (hábito pasado).

items.q: **Would** you like some coffee?

Condicional hipotético: would + verbo, con una condición (if) = situación hipotética. Acá tenés Would you like...? (ofrecimiento cortés).
Opinión suavizada: I would say / I would think = opinión más suave y menos directa. Acá tenés Would you like...? (ofrecimiento cortés).
Hábito pasado repetido: would + verbo (en pasado) = costumbre repetida de otra época. Acá tenés Would you like...? (ofrecimiento cortés).

items.q: I **would fix** that bug right now if I could.

Pedido formal / cortesía: Would you...? = pedido u ofrecimiento cortés. Acá tenés I would fix ... if I could (hipotético).
Opinión suavizada: I would say / I would think = opinión más suave y menos directa. Acá tenés I would fix ... if I could (hipotético).
Hábito pasado repetido: would + verbo (en pasado) = costumbre repetida de otra época. Acá tenés I would fix ... if I could (hipotético).

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
items.e: Modal + verbo base, sin to y sin -s.

después de un modal va el verbo base, sin to: must go.
los modales no llevan -s: must go.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:

después de can va el verbo base, sin to: can run.
los modales no llevan -s: can run.

items.q: Elegí la correcta (deducción negativa):
o: He mustn't be American. His English is terrible.
He can't be American. His English is terrible.
He doesn't must be American. His English is terrible.
items.a: He can't be American. His English is terrible.

He mustn't be American. His English is t: mustn't = prohibido; para deducir que es imposible se usa can't: He can't be American.
He doesn't must be American. His English: los modales no usan do/does: He can't be American.

items.q: Elegí la correcta (no es obligatorio):
o: You mustn't come to the meeting; it's optional.
You don't have to come to the meeting; it's optional.
You mustn't to come to the meeting; it's optional.
items.a: You don't have to come to the meeting; it's optional.
items.e: mustn't = prohibido; don't have to = no es necesario.

You mustn't come to the meeting; it's op: mustn't = prohibido; si es opcional, no es obligatorio: don't have to.
You mustn't to come to the meeting; it's: después de mustn't va el verbo base, sin to; y si es opcional: don't have to.

items.q: Elegí la correcta (hábito/estado pasado):
o: I would have a car when I was young.
I used to have a car when I was young.
I use to have a car when I was young.
items.a: I used to have a car when I was young.
items.e: would no aplica a estados (have); usá used to.

would no se usa con estados (have = tener): used to have.
en afirmativa el pasado es used (con d): used to have.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: She has to go home early.
She have to go home early.
items.a: She has to go home early.

has to + verbo; falta to: has to go.
she es 3.ª persona singular: has to.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: You had better to back up the files.
You had better back up the files.
You had better backing up the files.
items.a: You had better back up the files.

después de had better va el verbo base, sin to: had better back up.
después de had better va el verbo base: back up.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: She oughts to see a doctor.
She ought to see a doctor.
items.a: She ought to see a doctor.

ought to no lleva -s: ought to see.
ought lleva to: ought to see.

title: Modales en pasado: should have / must have / might have...
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. Pista: ¿crítica, deducción o necesidad en el pasado?

items.q: The programmer ___ made a mistake in the code. That's why the application crashed.
items.e: Deducción sobre el pasado → must have + participio.

must: must + verbo habla del presente; acá se deduce algo que ya pasó (the application crashed): must have + participio.
should: should = consejo/reproche; acá se deduce con casi seguridad lo que pasó: must have.
can: can habla de posibilidad en el presente; acá se deduce sobre el pasado: must have.

items.q: We ___ tested the new feature before releasing it. Now users are reporting problems.
items.e: Crítica: no lo hicimos y debimos → should have.

must: must have sería una deducción (seguro que lo probamos); acá es un reproche: Now users are reporting problems → should have.
can't: significado
can't have sería 'es imposible que lo probáramos'; acá es un reproche: should have.
might: might have = quizás lo hicimos; acá es un reproche por algo que no se hizo: should have.

items.q: The system was working perfectly yesterday, so the problem ___ happened during the update.

should: should have sería un reproche; acá se deduce con seguridad (funcionaba ayer): must have.
needn't: needn't have = no hacía falta hacerlo; no sirve para deducir: must have.
mustn't: mustn't = prohibido; no sirve para deducir: must have.

items.q: The programmer ___ forgotten to update the database.
items.e: Posibilidad en el pasado → may have + participio.

may: may + verbo habla del presente; acá es una posibilidad sobre el pasado: may have + participio.
should: should have sería un reproche, y la frase queda sin 'have'; la posibilidad: may have.
would: would no expresa posibilidad sobre el pasado: may have.

items.q: He ___ fixed the bug yesterday. He was on holiday.
items.e: Deducción negativa pasada → can't have (no mustn't have).

mustn't have: mustn't have no se usa para deducir; la deducción negativa en el pasado es can't have: He can't have fixed it.
shouldn't: shouldn't es un consejo/reproche y no encaja con 'estaba de vacaciones' (imposible que lo arreglara): can't have.
won't have: won't have habla del futuro/plan; acá es una deducción sobre el pasado: can't have.

items.q: We ___ informed the client about the delay earlier.

must: must (presente) no es un reproche sobre el pasado; hay que decir que no se hizo algo que convenía: should have.
can't: significado
can't no expresa reproche; es imposibilidad en el presente: should have.
mightn't: mightn't = quizás no; acá es un reproche: should have.

items.q: The developer ___ changed the code without telling the rest of the team.
items.e: Lo hizo y no debió → shouldn't have + participio.

mustn't: mustn't = prohibido en el presente; acá es un reproche sobre el pasado: shouldn't have.
can't: significado
can't = no se puede; acá se critica algo que ya hizo: shouldn't have.
needn't: needn't = no hace falta; acá es un reproche: shouldn't have.

items.q: The files aren't on the computer. Someone ___ deleted them accidentally.

must: must + verbo habla del presente; acá es una posibilidad sobre el pasado: might have + participio.
should: should have sería un reproche; acá es una posibilidad: might have.
can: can habla de posibilidad en el presente; sobre el pasado: might have.

items.q: I ___ worried about the test. I got 100%!
items.e: Te preocupaste y no hacía falta → needn't have + participio.

didn't need to: didn't need to = no era necesario (y quizás no lo hiciste). needn't have = lo hiciste y no hacía falta. Acá te preocupaste inútilmente: needn't have.
mustn't have: mustn't have no es una estructura usada; para algo hecho que no era necesario: needn't have.
couldn't: couldn't = no podía; acá es una preocupación que no hacía falta: needn't have.

items.q: The window was open when we arrived. Someone ___ forgotten to close it.

must: must + verbo habla del presente; acá se deduce sobre el pasado: must have + participio.
can't: significado
can't expresa imposibilidad; acá se deduce que seguro alguien lo hizo: must have.
should: should expresa consejo/reproche; acá es una deducción: must have.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:

should have va con participio: gone.
después de un modal va have, no has: should have gone.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: He must have go to the office.
He must have gone to the office.
He must has went to the office.
items.a: He must have gone to the office.

must have va con participio: gone.
después de un modal va have, y el participio de go es gone: must have gone.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:

needn't have va con participio: worried.

items.q: Elegí la que critica algo que SÍ hiciste (desplegaste un viernes):
o: You should have deployed on a Friday.
You shouldn't have deployed on a Friday.
You shouldn't deployed on a Friday.
items.a: You shouldn't have deployed on a Friday.
items.e: Lo hiciste y no debiste → shouldn't have.

should have = tendrías que haberlo hecho; acá se critica que SÍ lo hiciste: shouldn't have.
falta have + participio: shouldn't have deployed.

items.q: Elegí la que deduce sobre el pasado (a él le pidieron que se fuera):
o: He must be asked to leave.
He must have been asked to leave.
He must have asked to leave.
items.a: He must have been asked to leave.
items.e: Deducción pasada + pasiva → must have been + participio.

must be asked habla del presente; acá se deduce sobre el pasado: must have been asked.
pasiva incompleta: must have been asked (falta been).
